title: Google Sheets' new Gemini feature finally made me understand my finances
excerpt: Why I ditched formula troubleshooting for Gemini in Google Sheets
content_html:
Published Aug 7, 2026, 8:15 AM EDT

Dhruv Bhutani has covered the Android ecosystem since 2010, with a focus on smartphones, connected devices, and home networking. His reporting is informed by hands-on experience reviewing hundreds of smartphones and testing a wide range of smart home and audio products over more than a decade. He has attended Mobile World Congress eight times since 2011 and IFA Berlin five times, alongside regular coverage of launch events and industry briefings from companies including Google, Xiaomi, Oppo, and Qualcomm. This on-ground access and long-term exposure to product cycles inform how he evaluates hardware, software direction, and ecosystem shifts.

First-Hand Experience

Reviewed and tested hundreds of smartphones since 2009

Tested smart home, audio, and connected devices across multiple categories

Attended Mobile World Congress (8 times, first in 2011)

Attended IFA Berlin (5 times)

Covered industry events including Qualcomm Summit and launch events from Google, Xiaomi, Oppo, and Vivo

Career History

May 2024 – Present

November 2022 – Present

February 2010 – May 2011

Nokia Mobile Talk — Writer

June 2009 – October 2009

I've tracked my finances in Google Sheets for years. It gives me a lot more flexibility than any budgeting app I've tried.

The problem is that when I add something new, I have to dabble in formulas, and I was never particularly good at math.

When something breaks, figuring it out takes longer than analyzing my finances and takes me down a rabbit hole of Google searches.

That's why Google's new Gemini-powered Formula Fixes feature immediately caught my attention.

Instead of manually troubleshooting formulas or searching online for the right syntax, I can ask Gemini to identify and suggest a working fix.

It's been the easiest way for me to upgrade my financial tracking.

Formula Fixes explains my mistakes instead of leaving me with errors

Building a finance tracker that grows with my needs

What started as a simple spreadsheet of savings and investments has quickly grown into something much more than that for me.

Over the last year, I've been dabbling in proper expense tracking and keeping separate sheets for recurring bills, goals, and credit card payments.

As my finances become more detailed, I regularly add new calculations to make sure that I stay on track.

The other day, I wanted to calculate how much I spent on a recent trip, and all too often I'd scratch my head at the end of the month, wondering how much I spent on restaurants. And there are investments to keep tabs on.

To effectively use Google Sheets, you will want to combine several advanced spreadsheet functions.

I know the basics, but if you ask me about filter, query, index, or match functions, that's beyond my understanding.

Even a small mistake can completely upend your financial calculations. Google's Gemini-powered Formula Fixes changes that process.

Now, when a formula fails, Gemini analyzes not only the specific formula but also the data around it and helps me fix the problem.

Instead of showing me an error message, it points out if I referenced the wrong data range, selected incompatible data, or made a simple syntax error. It also suggests a corrected version that slots right into the spreadsheet.

But if the goal is to learn from your mistakes, Formula Fixes tells you exactly what you did wrong.

This ability to fix what I don't understand has allowed me to expand my tracker. I've added tabs that help me keep an eye on how much I've been spending on groceries and similar categories.

Additionally, you can ask Gemini to help you tabulate data or create a formula for a specific category or expense that you've set up.

It's also been helpful when manipulating data in older spreadsheets. Any time you move rows, columns, or reorganize things, the formula can stop working because the reference data has moved.

Now Gemini can help me identify these problems.

Gemini helps me understand my finances while fixing my formulas

I use Gemini to build dashboards I couldn't before

While Formula Fixes help me fix the issues in my spreadsheet, the addition of Gemini to Google Sheets has other benefits. It helps me focus and learn from my data, and this is something that AI is excellent at.

I'll give you an example. One section of my spreadsheet summarizes spending by category, while another compares my budget with what I actually spend each month. I also track my investments and emergency fund.

I've been using Gemini to create a dashboard that is full of formulas that pull information from individual sheets. Before I started using Gemini in Google Sheets, I had no idea how to pull this off.

So, I asked Gemini how to create a specific formula, and it gave me that. If the formula doesn't work because my data is structured in a way that is not conducive to it, Gemini and Formula Fixes will also explain that and recommend a correction.

It's been great for experimenting with my personal data.

I don't blindly trust this information. I still verify every important calculation, but it's helped me stop wasting time locating a misplaced bracket or incorrect range and instead focus on the important things, which is the actual data.

Formula Fixes lowers the learning curve for Google Sheets

In my finance tracking journey, I've come across some truly gifted spreadsheet wizards.

I always knew that Google Sheets was flexible enough to build exactly what I wanted, but I don't have the time to get a degree in Google Sheets. Gemini fixes that for me.

Formula Fixes solves the problem by explaining my errors in plain language and suggesting corrections based on the contents of my spreadsheet instead of me having to Google generic fixes.

That makes it easier to build a finance tracker that is specifically geared towards my use case. All in all, it's helped me make better financial decisions.

多年来我一直在 Google 表格中跟踪我的财务状况。 与我尝试过的任何预算应用程序相比，它为我提供了更多的灵活性。

问题是，当我添加新东西时，我必须涉足公式，而且我从来都不是特别擅长数学。

当出现问题时，弄清楚它比分析我的财务状况要花费更长的时间，并且会让我陷入谷歌搜索的兔子洞。

这就是为什么谷歌新推出的由 Gemini 驱动的 Formula Fixes 功能立即引起了我的注意。

我可以要求 Gemini 识别并建议可行的修复方案，而不是手动排除公式故障或在线搜索正确的语法。

这是我升级财务跟踪的最简单方法。

公式修复解释了我的错误，而不是让我留下错误

构建一个随着我的需求而增长的财务追踪器

一开始只是一个简单的储蓄和投资电子表格，但很快就发展成为比我更重要的东西。

在过去的一年里，我一直在尝试适当的费用跟踪，并为经常性账单、目标和信用卡付款保留单独的表格。

随着我的财务状况变得更加详细，我会定期添加新的计算以确保我保持在正轨上。

有一天，我想计算一下我最近一次旅行花了多少钱，而到了月底我常常会摸不着头脑，想知道我在餐馆上花了多少钱。 还有一些投资需要密切关注。

为了有效地使用 Google 表格，您需要结合多种高级电子表格功能。

我知道基础知识，但如果你问我有关过滤器、查询、索引或匹配函数的问题，那超出了我的理解范围。

即使是一个小错误也可能完全颠覆您的财务计算。 谷歌的 Gemini 支持的 Formula Fixes 改变了这个过程。

现在，当公式失败时，Gemini 不仅会分析具体公式，还会分析其周围的数据，并帮助我解决问题。

它不会向我显示错误消息，而是指出我是否引用了错误的数据范围、选择了不兼容的数据或犯了简单的语法错误。 它还建议了一个可以直接插入电子表格的更正版本。

但如果目标是从错误中吸取教训，公式修复会准确地告诉您做错了什么。

这种解决我不理解的问题的能力使我能够扩展我的跟踪器。 我添加了标签，帮助我关注我在杂货和类似类别上的花费。

此外，您可以要求 Gemini 帮助您将数据制成表格或为您设置的特定类别或费用创建公式。

在操作旧电子表格中的数据时，它也很有帮助。 每当您移动行、列或重新组织内容时，公式都可能停止工作，因为参考数据已移动。

现在 Gemini 可以帮我找出这些问题。

Gemini 帮助我了解我的财务状况，同时修正我的公式

我使用 Gemini 构建了以前无法构建的仪表板

虽然公式修复可以帮助我解决电子表格中的问题，但将 Gemini 添加到 Google 表格还有其他好处。 它帮助我集中注意力并从数据中学习，而这正是人工智能所擅长的。

我给你举个例子。 我的电子表格的一部分按类别总结支出，而另一部分将我的预算与我每月的实际支出进行比较。 我还跟踪我的投资和应急基金。

我一直在使用 Gemini 创建一个仪表板，其中充满了从各个工作表中提取信息的公式。 在我开始在 Google 表格中使用 Gemini 之前，我不知道如何实现这一目标。

所以，我问 Gemini 如何创建一个特定的公式，它给了我这个。 如果公式不起作用，因为我的数据结构不利于它，Gemini 和 Formula Fixes 也会对此进行解释并建议更正。

这对于试验我的个人数据非常有用。

我不会盲目相信这些信息。 我仍然验证每一个重要的计算，但这帮助我不再浪费时间查找放错位置的括号或不正确的范围，而是专注于重要的事情，即实际数据。

公式修复降低了 Google 表格的学习曲线

在我的财务跟踪之旅中，我遇到了一些真正有天赋的电子表格向导。

我一直都知道 Google 表格足够灵活，可以准确构建我想要的内容，但我没有时间获得 Google 表格学位。 双子座帮我解决了这个问题。

公式修复通过用简单的语言解释我的错误并根据电子表格的内容建议更正来解决问题，而不是我必须谷歌通用修复。

这使得构建专门针对我的用例的财务跟踪器变得更加容易。 总而言之，它帮助我做出了更好的财务决策。
